x: God Almighty says: The revelation of the Book which We sent down to you, O Muhammad, is from God, the Exalted in Might in His vengeance against His enemies, the Wise in His management of His creation, not from anyone else, so do not be in doubt about that. He raised His statement the revelation with His statement from God. The interpretation of the statement is: from God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, the revelation of the Book. It is permissible to raise it by implying this, as it was said: A Surah We have sent down (al-Nur 24:1). However, raising it in His statement the revelation of the Book with what comes after it is better than raising a surah with what comes after it, because tanzil is a verb, but it is closer to being definite, since it is added to a definite noun, so raising it with what comes after it is good, but that is not good in a surah, because it is indefinite.

And His statement, Indeed, We have sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Indeed, We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, the Book, meaning by the Book: the Qur'an, in truth, meaning in justice. He says: We sent down to you this Qur'an that commands truth and justice, and part of that truth and justice is that you worship God, devoting your religion to Him alone, because religion is for Him, not for idols that do not possess the power to harm or benefit. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of His saying the Book, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, meaning: the Qur’an. And His statement, Worship God, devoting your religion to Him, the Almighty says: So, O Muhammad, be humble before God by obeying Him, and be sincere in your deity to Him, and worship Him alone, and do not make any partner with Him in your worship of Him, as the idol worshippers did. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated: Yaqub narrated to us, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of Shamir, who said: A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection for judgment, and in his record of good deeds will be mountains of good deeds. The Lord of Glory, the Majestic and the Exalted, will say: I prayed on such-and-such a day so that it would be said, ‘So-and-so prayed. I am God, there is no god but Me, for Me is the pure religion.’ I fasted on such-and-such a day so that it would be said, ‘So-and-so fasted. I am God, there is no god but Me, for Me is the pure religion.’ I gave charity on such-and-such a day so that it would be said, ‘So-and-so gave charity. I am God, there is no god but Me, for Me is the pure religion.’ Then He will continue to erase one thing after another until his record of deeds remains with nothing on it. Then His two angels will say: ‘O so-and-so, did you do anything other than God?’

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: as for his saying sincerely devoting religion to Him, it means monotheism, and religion is in the accusative case because of the verb sincerely being applied to it.

x: And His statement, Surely, to God belongs the pure religion, God Almighty says: Surely, to God belongs worship and obedience alone, with no partner, pure, with no partner for anyone with Him in it. This is not appropriate for anyone, because everything below Him belongs to Him, and the slave must obey his owner, not someone who does not own anything of it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

m: Surely, the pure religion belongs to God is the testimony that there is no god but God. And His statement,

I have explained that in its place previously.

x: God Almighty says: He created you, O people, from one soul, meaning from Adam. Then He created from it its mate. He says: Then He created from Adam his mate, Eve, and that is because God created her from one of his ribs. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

x: If someone were to say, “How is it said, ‘
h

, then made from him his mate,’ when the children of Adam were created from Adam and his wife, and there is no doubt that the parents come before the children?” There are several opinions on that. One of them is that it was said that it was said because it was narrated from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him): When God created Adam, He smoothed his back and brought forth every soul that will exist until the Day of Resurrection. Then He settled him in Paradise after that, and after that He created Eve from one of his ribs. This is an opinion. The other is that the Arabs would sometimes describe a man with two verbs, repeating the first of them in meaning with then, if it is from the first-person report, as one says, What happened to you today has reached me, and What happened to you yesterday is more amazing.
This is in line with the first-person report.

i: The other aspect: that His creation of the pair is attributed to one of them, as if it were said: He created you from a single soul and then made its mate from it, so in one there is the meaning: He created it alone, as the rajaz poet said:

And His statement, God of the Kingdom, means, “The Lord of your Lord, O people, whose description is what He has described to you, and whose power is what He has made clear to you, is the Kingdom of this world and the Hereafter and their authority, and no one else’s. As for the kings of this world, one of them only owns something and not something else, so he only has a special portion of the Kingdom. As for the complete Kingdom, which is the Kingdom in absolute terms, it is for God, the One, the Prevailing.” And His statement, There is no god but Him, so how are you turned away? God Almighty says: There should be no god but Him, and worship is only appropriate for Him. So how are you turned away? God Almighty says: So how are you turned away, O people, so that you turn away from the worship of your Lord, whose attribute is this, to the worship of One from Whom you can neither harm nor benefit. , and He will inform you about what you used to do. God the Almighty says: Then, after you have done in this world what you did of good and bad, faith and disbelief, O people, to your Lord is your return after your death. He will inform you: He says: He will tell you what you used to do in this world of good and evil, and He will reward you for all of that with your reward, the good among you according to his goodness, and the evildoer according to what he deserves. God the Almighty says to His servants: So fear that you will meet your Lord while you have done in this world what He does not approve of, lest you perish, for nothing of the deeds of any of you is hidden from Him. And His statement, Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts, means that God Almighty says: Indeed, nothing is hidden from God, O people, that which your breasts conceal, which your eyes cannot perceive, so how about what the eyes perceive and the sight see? What He, the Almighty, means by this statement is that nothing is hidden from Him, and that He is the One who records the deeds of His servants, to reward them for them so that they may fear Him in their secret and public affairs.

x: God the Almighty says: And when a person is touched by a calamity in his body, such as sickness, disability, hardship in his livelihood, effort and distress, “he calls upon his Lord meaning: he seeks help from his Lord who created him from the severity of that, and asks Him to relieve him of the severity of that which has befallen him. And His statement turning to Him means: repenting to Him for what he was doing before that, such as disbelief in Him, and associating deities and idols with Him in worship, returning to His obedience. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And when harm touches man

, he said: pain, affliction, and hardship. He calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance, he said: seeking His help. And His statement, Then if He bestows upon him a blessing from Himself, the Most High says: Then if his Lord bestows upon him a blessing from Himself, meaning well-being, and removes his harm, and replaces sickness with health, and hardship with ease. The Arabs say to everyone who gives another wealth or other things: He bestowed upon him, and from this is the saying of Abu al-Najm al-‘Ijli: He gave and did not withhold, nor was he stingy. The heap of grains is from the wealth of the one who is given.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah Ma’mar ibn al-Muthanna that he said:
m: I heard Abu Amr say in the verse of Zuhair: If they are given money, they are given it. If they are asked, they are given it. If they are given money, they are given it. Muammar said: Yunus said: We only heard it: If they are fooling around with money, they will be fooled. He said: It has the same meaning. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: Then if He bestows upon him a blessing from Him: if He bestows upon him health or goodness. His saying,
h
He forgot what

he used to call for before, means: He abandoned his supplication to God before He removed the harm that he was suffering from. And he made equals to God, meaning: partners. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: He forgot means: he left. This is specifically for the unbeliever. As for the word ma in His statement,
h
He forgot what

was, there are two interpretations: One of them is that it means who, and the meaning of the statement then is: He abandoned the one he used to call upon in the state of distress he was in, meaning by that God, the Most High. So ma is in this case the place of min, as it was said, Nor do you worship that which I worship (al-Kafirun 109:3), meaning God, and as it was said, Then marry such women as seem good to you. The second is that it means the source, as I mentioned. If it means the source, then the ha in His statement, to Him has two interpretations: One of them is that it is from the mention of ma, and the other is from the mention of the Lord. His saying,
h
And He has made equals to God
, means: He has made similarities and likenesses to God. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning in which they made them rivals to Him.

x: Some of them said: They made them rivals to Him in their obedience to Him in disobeying God.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
And He has made equals to God
. He said: The equals are men, who obey them in disobeying God.

x: Others said: What he meant by that was that he worshipped idols, and made them rivals to God in their worship of them. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: What is meant by it is Surat al-Zumar 39:8
h
And when harm touches man

, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then, when He bestows upon him a favor from Himself, he forgets what he used to call upon Him for before and sets up equals to God to mislead [man] from His way. Say, "
h
Enjoy your disbelief

for a little; indeed, you are among the companions of the Fire." that he obeyed Satan in worshipping idols, and thus made idols equal to him, because that was in the context of God’s rebuke of them to him for worshipping them. And His statement, to mislead [others] from His way, means: to prevent those who wanted to believe in God and to unify Him from believing in Him, acknowledging Him, and entering Islam.
And His statement, Say, ‘
h
Enjoy your disbelief
for a little while,’ means that God Almighty is saying to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say, O Muhammad, to the one who does that:
h
Enjoy your disbelief

in God for a little while until your appointed time is fulfilled, and then your death comes to you. Indeed, you are among the companions of the Fire, meaning that you are among the people of the Fire who will abide in it. And His statement,
h
Enjoy your disbelief
, is a warning and a threat from God.
The reciters differed in their reading of His statement Aman.

Some of the Meccans, some of the Medinans, and most of the Kufians read it as Aman with a light mim. There are two aspects to their reading of it: One of them is that the alif in Aman means supplication, and what is meant by it is: O He who is devout during the hours of the night. The Arabs call out with the alif as they call out with ya, so they say: Azayd is approaching, and O Zayd is approaching. From this is the saying of Aws ibn Hajar: My sons, you are not one hand but a hand that has no arm. And if the alif is directed to the vocative, the meaning of the speech is: Say, O disbeliever, enjoy your disbelief for a little, for you are among the companions of the Fire. And O you who are despairing during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, for you are among the people of Paradise. And he will be in the Fire. What the disbelieving group will have with God as a reward in the Hereafter is sufficient to explain what the believing group will have, since it is known that their conditions are different in this world, and it is reasonable that if one of them is among the companions of the Fire due to his disbelief in his Lord, then the other is among the companions of Paradise.

So the report of what he has is omitted, as it is sufficient for the listener to understand what is meant by it from its mention, since it had indicated what was omitted by what was mentioned. The second: that the alif in his statement amn is an alif of interrogation, so the meaning of the speech is: Is this like the one who has set up rivals to God to lead [people] astray from His path?

i: Then it is sufficient with what preceded from God’s report about the group of disbelievers from His enemies, since the intended meaning of the speech was understood, as the poet said:
x: I swear that if anything came to us from his messenger other than you, we would not have found a defense against you.
So he deleted the word to pay it and it was intended in the speech since the listener understood what he meant.

Some of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa read it as Aman with a shaddah on the mim, meaning: Or who is he? They say: It is Aman an interrogative that came into the speech after a previous statement, so Am was used. According to this interpretation, the answer to the interrogative must be left out because the report had been made about the group of disbelievers and what was prepared for them in the hereafter, then the report was followed by the report about the group of believers, so the intended meaning was known, so the listener’s knowledge of its meaning was sufficient from what was mentioned, since it was reasonable that its meaning is better, or this one. Our opinion on this matter is that they are two readings, each of which was recited by scholars of the Qur’an reciters5, with each of them being correct in interpretation and grammar. So whichever of the two the reciter recites, he is correct.

We have already mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differed, and the correct opinion in our view regarding the meaning of al-Qanit in what has passed before, so there is no need to repeat it here. However, we will mention some of the statements of the people of interpretation regarding that in this place, so that the one who looks into the Book will know that the meaning is the same in this place and others.
Some of them said: In this place it is the recitation of the reader while standing in prayer.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Ubayd God, that he said: Nafi’ told me, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: that when he was asked about Qunut, he would say: I do not know of Qunut except for the recitation of the Qur’an and prolonged standing, and he would recite: Is he who is devout during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing?

x: It is obedience. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His statement, Is one who is devoutly obedient?

He means by devoutly obedient, as He said, Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you will come forth (ar-Rum 30:25) . . . to All are devoutly obedient to Him (ar-Rum 30:26), he said: Obedient.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Or is he who is devout during the hours of the night
, prostrating and standing? He said: The devout is the obedient. His saying at night means: the hours of the night.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Is he who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night and for him
, and the middle of it, and the end of it.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: The hours of the night means the hours of the night. We have already explained the meaning of the hours with supporting evidence and narrated the statements of the scholars of interpretation concerning it, making it unnecessary to repeat it here. And his saying, prostrating and standing, means: he prays while prostrating sometimes, and while standing sometimes, meaning: he obeys, and qunut in our view means obedience, and for this reason his saying, prostrating and standing, is in the accusative case because its meaning is: who prays during the hours of the night, prostrating sometimes, and standing sometimes, so they are the states of the one who prays. And his saying, warns of the Hereafter, means: he fears the punishment of the Hereafter. Like: Ali narrated to us on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Azdi, he said:

c: Yahya bin Al-Yaman narrated to us, on the authority of Ash'ath, on the authority of Ja'far, on the authority of Sa'id bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God, and fears the Hereafter, he said: He fears the punishment of the Hereafter, and hopes for the mercy of his Lord, meaning: and hopes that God will have mercy on him and admit him into Paradise. And His statement, Say, 'Are those who know equal to those who do not know?' God, the Exalted, says: Say, O Muhammad, to your al-Nas 114:Are those equal to those who know the reward for their obedience to their Lord and the consequences for their disobedience to Him, and those who do not know that? So they wander aimlessly, neither hoping for good from their good deeds nor fearing evil from their bad deeds? God says: These two are not equal.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Jaafar Muhammad bin Ali
m: regarding this matter: Muhammad bin Khalaf told me, he said: Nasr bin Muzahim told me, he said: Sufyan Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Mujahid, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, may God be pleased with him: Are those who know equal to those who do not know? He said: We are the ones who know, and our enemy is the ones who do not know. And His statement,
h
Only those with understanding will remember
, God Almighty says: Only those with reason and wisdom will consider God’s proofs, learn from them, reflect on them, and ponder them, not those with ignorance and deficient minds.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement Aman.
Some of the Meccans, some of the Medinans, and most of the Kufians read it as Aman with a light mim.
There are two aspects to their reading of it: One of them is that the alif in Aman means supplication, and what is meant by it is: O He who is devout during the hours of the night.
Some of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa read it as Aman with a shaddah on the mim, meaning: Or who is he?
Our opinion on this matter is that they are two readings, each of which was recited by scholars of the Qur’an reciters5, with each of them being correct in interpretation and grammar.
Some of them said: In this place it is the recitation of the reader while standing in prayer.

Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Ubayd God, that he said: Nafi’ told me, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that when he was asked about Qunut, he would say: I do not know of Qunut except for the recitation of the Qur’an and prolonged standing, and he would recite: Is he who is devout during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing?

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to My servants who have believed: O My servants who have believed, in God and believed in His Messenger, fear your Lord, by obeying Him and avoiding His disobedience. For those who do good in this world is good. Then the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that, some of them said: Its meaning is: for those who obeyed God there is good in this world, and he said in the connection of good, and he made the meaning of good: health and wellness.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad told us: Ahmad told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: For those who do good in this world is good. He said: Well-being and health.

x: Others said that the connection between they did well is related to the good, and the meaning of good is paradise. And His saying,
h
And the earth of God is spacious
, God Almighty says:
h
And the earth of God is spacious
and wide, so they migrated from the land of polytheism to the abode of Islam.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And the earth of God is spacious
, so they migrated and abandoned the idols. And His statement,
h
Only those who are patient will be given their reward in full

, without account, God Almighty says: God only gives those who are patient in what they encounter in this world their reward in the Hereafter, without account. He says: Their reward is without account. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Only the patient will be given their reward in full, without account. No, by God, there is no measure or scale for you.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Only the patient will be given their reward in full, without account. He said: In Paradise.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your al-Nas 114:God has commanded me to worship Him alone, obedience to Him alone, without all the gods and rivals that you call upon besides Him.

And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims: He says: And my Lord, may He be glorified, commanded me to do that, so that by doing that I would be the first of you to submit to Him, submit to Him in monotheism, devote worship to Him, and disavow all deities besides Him.

And the Almighty’s saying, Say, ‘Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.’ God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to them, Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord in what He has commanded me to do of worshipping Him, sincerely obeying Him and singling Him out as Lord. “The punishment of a tremendous Day” means the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, that is the day whose terror is most great.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your al-Nas 114:I worship God sincerely, devoting my obedience and worship to Him alone. I do not make any partner for Him in that, but I single Him out as divinity, and I disavow Him of all rivals and gods besides Him.

So worship, O people, whatever you wish of idols and statues, and other than that which you worship from the rest of His creation, for you will know the consequences of your worship of that when you meet your Lord. And His statement, Say, ‘Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves,’ God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to them: Indeed, the lost are those who have deceived themselves, and their families have been destroyed by God’s punishment along with themselves, so when they entered the Fire they had no family in it, while they had family in this world. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Say, ‘Indeed, the losers are those who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.’ He said: They are the disbelievers whom God created for the Fire, and created the Fire for them, so the world was taken away from them, and Paradise was forbidden to them. God said, He will lose this world and the Hereafter (al-Hajj 22:11).

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Say, ‘Indeed, the losers are those who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection,’ he said: These are the people of Hellfire. They lost themselves in this world and lost their families, so they did not find people in Hellfire, although they had people in this world.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Zaydah, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: They have deceived themselves and their families. He said: They will lose their families, so they will have no family to return to, and they will lose themselves, so they will perish in the Fire, and they will die while they are alive, so they will lose both of them. And His statement, Indeed, that is the manifest loss, God Almighty says: Indeed, the loss of these polytheists is themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection, and that is their destruction, which is the manifest loss. God Almighty says: It is the destruction that is clear to whoever witnesses it and knows that it is the loss.

x: God Almighty says: For these losers on the Day of Resurrection in Hell, above them are shades of fire, which is like shades built from fire, and beneath them are shades, meaning: and beneath them are shades of fire that rise above them, until what is above them becomes shades beneath them. This is similar to His Most High saying: For them is a bed of Hell, and above them is covering that covers them from what is beneath them in it of the bed. And His statement, “
h
This is what God frightens His servants with

. O My servants, then fear Me.” God Almighty says: This, O people, that which I have informed you of, of the torment for the losers on the Day of Resurrection, is a warning from your Lord to you, by which He frightens you so that you may beware of Him, avoid His transgressions, and turn from your disbelief to belief in Him, and confirmation of His Messenger, and following His commands and prohibitions, so that you may be saved from His punishment in the Hereafter. Then fear Me. He says: Then fear Me by fulfilling My obligations upon you and avoiding My transgressions, so that you may be saved from My punishment and wrath.
And His statement,
h
And those who avoid Taghut

: meaning, they avoid the worship of everything that is worshipped other than God. We have already explained the meaning of Taghut previously with evidence for that, and we have mentioned the differences of opinion among the people of interpretation concerning it, so there is no need to repeat it here. We have mentioned that in this instance it refers to Satan, and in this instance and elsewhere it has one meaning according to us.
Mention of those who said what we mentioned in this place:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And those who avoid Taghut
, he said: Satan.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
And those who avoid Taghut
by worshipping it, he said: Satan.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And those who avoid Taghut

, lest they worship it, he said: The devil here is one and it is a group, and Taghut, according to this statement of Ibn Zayd, is one and feminine, and that is why it was said: lest they worship it. And it was said: It is made feminine because it has the meaning of a group. His saying,
h
And they turned to God

, means: They repented to God and returned to acknowledging His Oneness, working to obey Him, and disavowing all other gods and rivals besides Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And they turned to God
h
and they turned to God

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And they turned to God
, he said: They responded to Him. And his saying,
h
For them is good report
, means:
h
For them is good report
of this world and Paradise in the Hereafter.

x: So give good tidings to My servants * who listen to the word God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So give good tidings, O Muhammad, to My servants who listen to the word of the speakers, and follow the most correct and most guided of them, and the evidence of the oneness of God, and of working in obedience to Him, and they leave aside what is other than that of the word that does not indicate right guidance, nor does it guide to the right path. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they follow the best of it, and the best of it is obedience to God.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement, and they follow the best of it, he said: The best of what they are commanded to do, so they act upon it. And His statement,
h
Those are the ones whom God has guided

, means, those who listen to the word and follow the best of it—those whom God has guided, meaning, May God guide them to the right path and to what is correct, not those who turn away from hearing the truth and worship that which neither harms nor benefits. And His statement,
h
Those are the ones with understanding

, means, those with reason and discernment. He mentioned that this verse was revealed about a well-known group who believed in the oneness of God and disavowed the worship of anything other than God before the Prophet of God was sent. So God revealed this verse to His Prophet to praise them.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And those who avoid Taghut

, lest they worship it . . . the two verses, my father told me that these two verses were revealed about three men who used to say, There is no god but God in the pre-Islamic era: Zayd ibn Amr, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, and Salman al-Farsi. The verse,
h
And those who avoid Taghut

, lest they worship it in their pre-Islamic era “and turn back to God for them is good tidings. So give good tidings to My servants * Those who listen to the word and follow the best of it” “There is no god but God.
h
Those are the ones whom God has guided
without a scripture or a prophet. And those are the ones of understanding.”

x: He, the Most High, means by His saying,
h
Is he upon whom the word of punishment has come due
h
Is he upon whom the word of punishment has come due
in the foreknowledge of your Lord, O Muhammad, because of his disbelief in Him?

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Is he upon whom the word of punishment has come due
because of his disbelief. And His statement,
h
Will you then save those in the Fire

? God the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him): Will you, O Muhammad, save those who are in the Fire from whom the word of punishment has been justified? You will save him. So His statement,
h
Will you then save those in the Fire
, dispenses with this.

x: Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: This is one of the things that is intended as a single question, so the question is rushed to the wrong place, and the question is returned to its proper place. Rather, the meaning, and God knows best, is:
h
Will you then save those in the Fire
from whom the word of punishment has been justified? He said: And similar to it, other than a question, is: Does He promise you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth?
r
(Al-Mu'minun 23:35)

, so He repeated you twice. The meaning, and God knows best, is: Does He promise you that you will be brought forth when you die? And similar to it is His statement, Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done - do not think that they are beyond the reach of the punishment.
r
(Al-Imran 3:188)
Some of them considered the statement we have related from the Basrans to be incorrect, and said that the statement,
h
Will you then save those in the Fire

? should not be a metaphor for someone who came before. It should not be said, The people struck those who stood up. The meaning is, “The division. Will you then save those of them who are in the Fire?” Rather, the meaning of the statement is, Will you, O Muhammad, guide someone who was previously known by God to be among the people of the Fire to faith, and save him from the Fire through faith? You are not capable of that.
And His statement,
h
But those who feared their Lord
, for them are mansions, above which are mansions built. God Almighty says:
h
But those who feared their Lord

, by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, for them in Paradise are mansions, above which are mansions built, one above the other. Underneath which rivers flow. God Almighty says: Rivers flow beneath the trees of its gardens. And His statement,
h
The promise of God

, God Almighty says: We have promised these mansions, above which are mansions built in Paradise, to these righteous ones. God does not fail in His promise. God Almighty says: God does not fail to fulfill His promise to them.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, that God sends down water from the sky, meaning rain, and causes it to flow as springs in the earth, meaning: He causes it to flow as springs in the earth. One of them is a spring, which is what gushes from the earth. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding the statement, And He caused springs to flow through the earth, he said: Every dew and water on the earth descended from the sky. He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muslim bin Bayan, who said: Then He caused to grow with that water which He sent down from the sky and made it springs in the earth, crops of varying colors, meaning: different types of wheat, barley, sesame, rice, and other different types like that. Then it withers and you see it yellow, meaning: Then that crop dries up after its greenness. It is said of the earth when what is in it of greenery and withers dries up: the earth is agitated, and the crops are agitated. His statement, and you see it yellow, means: you see it dry and yellow after its greenness and moisture. Similarly, crops turn yellow when they dry. Then He makes it into fragments. The fragments are the crumbs of straw and hay. He says: Then He makes that crop after it has become dry and crumbly. And His statement,
h
Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding

, the Most High says: Indeed in God’s action for you as described is a reminder and an admonition for the people of reason and wisdom, so that they may remember by it and know that whoever does that will not be unable to bring into existence whatever things He wills, and create whatever bodies and accidents He wants, and to revive whoever perishes, creating him after his death and returning him after his annihilation to the state he had before his annihilation, like what He did with the earth upon which He sent down water after its death, and caused plants of different colors to grow in it by His power.

x: God Almighty says: Is he whose heart God has expanded to know Him, acknowledge His Oneness, submit to His Lordship, and submit to His obedience so he is upon a light from his Lord? He says: So he has insight into what he is and certainty, through the illumination of the Truth in his heart, and therefore follows God’s commands and refrains from what He has forbidden in a way that pleases Him, like he whose heart God has hardened, emptied of His remembrance, and made narrow to listen to the truth, follow guidance, and act according to what is right? Leaving out the one whose heart God has hardened and the answer to the question is sufficient for the listeners to know what is intended by the statement, since He mentioned one of the two types, and replaced the mention of the other type with the report about it by His statement:
h
So woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of God
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Is he whose breast God has expanded to Islam so that he is upon a light from his Lord
? means: The Book of God is the believer, he takes it and ends up with it.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Is he whose breast God has expanded to Islam
? He said: He has expanded his breast to Islam, and light means guidance.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Zaydah, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
Is he whose breast God has expanded to Islam
? He said: The one whose breast is expanded is not like the one whose heart is hard. His statement,
h
So woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of God

Surat al-Zumar 39:23

? He said: He will fall on his face into the Fire. He says: It is like Is he who is thrown into the Fire better or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?
r
(Fussilat 41:40)

x: Others said: It means that he will be taken to the fire, bound, then thrown into it, and the first thing the fire will touch will be his face. This is a statement that is mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas from a source that I hated to mention because of the weakness of its chain of transmission. And His statement, And it will be said to the wrongdoers, ‘Taste what you used to earn.’ He says: On that day it will be said to the wrongdoers themselves, because they earned God’s wrath: Taste today, O people, the evil of what you used to earn in this world of disobeying God.
And His statement,
h

, God Almighty says: Those before these polytheists from Quraysh, from the nations who passed away in the past, denied their messengers. So the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive, meaning: So God’s punishment came to them from a place where they did not perceive: meaning they did not know that it would come from.

God Almighty says: So God hastened for these nations who denied His messengers humiliation in this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and He did not respite them when they rebelled against the command of their Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater. x: God the Almighty says: God gives an example of a disbeliever who worships various gods and obeys a group of devils, and a believer who worships only the One God. God the Almighty says:
h
God sets forth an example

for this disbeliever, a man who has partners. He says: He is among a group of quarreling owners, meaning different and in conflict, with bad morals, from their saying: a man of bad character, if he has bad morals and each one of them uses him according to his share and ownership in him. And a man who is at peace with another, He says: and a man who is purely devoted to another, meaning the believer who is monotheistic and who has sincerely devoted his worship to God, who does not worship anyone other than Him and does not owe any lordship to anything other than Him. The reciters differed in their reading of the verse, and a healthy man.
Some of the reciters from Mecca and Basra read it as a healthy man, and they interpreted it to mean: a man who is purely for a man. This was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told us: Al-Qasim told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Jarir bin Hazim, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that he read it as salman li-rajul meaning with an alif, and he said: There is nothing in it for anyone. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it as wa rajul salman li-rajul meaning: in peace. The correct view in this regard, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings, each of which has been recited by scholars of the Qur’an, and they are close in meaning. Whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. This is because as-Salam is a verbal noun derived from the saying: So-and-so submitted to God as-Salam, meaning: he was sincerely devoted to Him. The Arabs say: So-and-so made a profit in his trade, and He submitted as-Salam, “Salam,” and Safety. Safe is an attribute of a man, and as-Salam is a verbal noun derived from that. As for what was imagined by those who avoided reading it as as-Salam, that it means peace, there is no basis for peace in this instance, because what preceded as an attribute of the other was only preceded by the report of a group participating in it, not the report of his war with something. So the report should be about his opponent being sincere to One with no partner, and there is no place for the report of war and peace in this instance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, “God presents a parable: a man with partners at variance with one another, and a man who is entirely at peace with one another,” he said: Have you seen the man who has partners at variance with one another, all of them bad in character, and you will find him taking a portion of the wealth to be used by the worst of them, and which only one of them owns? . He said: Is the one about whom there is disagreement better, or the one about whom there is no disagreement? His saying,

Praise be to God
, means: complete thanks and perfect praise are due to God alone, without any other deity besides Him. His saying,
h
But most of them do not know

, means, This which is shared is not equal to that which is unique and belongs to One. Rather, most of these polytheists do not know that they are not equal, so in their ignorance of that, they worship various gods besides God. It was said, Are they equal in comparison? He did not say, Two examples, because they both set one example, so the example was based on monotheism, as God, the Most High, said, And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign. (al-Mu’minun 23:50), since their meaning was one in the verse. And God knows best.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: You, Muhammad, will die soon, and those who denied you from your people, including the believers among them, will die. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will all dispute before your Lord. He says: Then on the Day of Resurrection you, believers and disbelievers, will all dispute before your Lord, and He will take from the oppressed among you for the oppressor, and He will judge between all of you with justice. The commentators differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said: It refers to the dispute between the believers and the unbelievers, and the dispute between the oppressed and the oppressor.
Who said that?

c: Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then on the Day of Resurrection you will dispute before your Lord
, he said: The truthful will dispute with the liar, the oppressed with the oppressor, the guided with the misguided, and the weak with the arrogant.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
Then on the Day of Resurrection you will dispute before your Lord
, he said: The people of Islam and the people of disbelief.

c: Ibn al-Barqi told me: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Ibn al-Darwardi told us: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said:
m: When this verse was revealed: “Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die. Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, you will dispute before your Lord,” al-Zubayr said: O Messenger of God, will what happened between us in this world be denied us, along with our special sins? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, until everyone who has a right is given his right.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant by that the dispute of the people of Islam.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, who said:
m: This verse was revealed to us, and we did not know its interpretation until the tribulation occurred. We said: This is what our Lord promised us that we would dispute about.
h
Then on the Day of Resurrection you will dispute before your Lord

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: When the verse, “Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die. Then indeed, you will…” was revealed, they said: What is our dispute among us, since we are brothers? He said: When Uthman ibn Affan was killed, they said: This is our dispute among us.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Then on the Day of Resurrection you will dispute before your Lord

, he said: The people of the Qiblah. The most correct of the sayings about this is to say: He meant by that: You, O Muhammad, will die, and you, O people, will die, and then all of you, O people, will dispute before your Lord, your believers and your unbelievers, your truthful and your false, your oppressors and your oppressed, until each of you is given his due from the one who owes him his due. We said that this statement is more correct because God, in His statement:
h
Then on the Day of Resurrection you will surely dispute before your Lord

, is addressing all of His servants. He did not specify some of them over others, so this is based on its generality based on what God made it general. A verse may have been revealed for one meaning, and then everything that was in the meaning of the one for which it was revealed is included in its ruling.

x: Then on the Day of Resurrection you will dispute before your Lord.
And His statement:
h
Who is more unjust than he who lies about God and denies the truth when it comes to him

? God Almighty says: Who created God is more slanderous than he who lies about God, claiming that He has a son and a wife, or that he forbade food that which He did not forbid? And denies the truth when it comes to him means: And denies the Book of God when He revealed it to Muhammad, and God sent him with it as a Messenger, and denied the statement, There is no god but God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And he denied the truth when it came to him: meaning the Qur’an. And His statement:
h
Is there not in Hell a place of refuge for the disbelievers

? God Almighty says: Is there not in Hell a refuge and a dwelling place for those who disbelieve in God and refuse to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his followers in what he called them to, which he brought to them from God of monotheism and the rulings of the Qur’an?

x: The people of interpretation differed about the one who brought the truth and who believed in it, and who that was.

Some of them said: The one who brought the truth was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The truth that he brought was: There is no god but God, and the one who believed in it also is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And he who brought the truth
means: he who came with there is no god but God “
h
and believed in it
” meaning his Messenger.

x: Others said: The one who brought the truth was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the one who believed in it was Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad bin Mansour told me, he said: Ahmad bin Masʿad Al-Marwazi told us, he said: Umar bin Ibrahim bin Khalid told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Asid bin Safwan, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement:
h
And he who brought the truth
, he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
h
And believed in it
, he said: Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him.

x: Others said: The one who brought the truth is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the truth is the Qur’an, and those who believe in it are the believers.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And he who brought the truth
means: This is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who came with the Qur’an, and the believers believed in it.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And he who brought the truth is the Messenger of God
, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims believed in him.

x: Others said: The one who brought the truth was Gabriel, and the truth is the Qur’an that he brought from God, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, believed in it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And he who brought the truth and believed in it Muhammad
, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Others said that the one who brought the truth is the believers, and the truth is the Qur’an, and they are those who believe in it.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And he who brought the truth and believed in it

, he said: Those who come with the Qur’an on the Day of Resurrection and say: This is what you gave us, so we followed what was in it. He said: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
And he who brought the truth and believed in it

, he said: They are the people of the Qur’an who will come with it on the Day of Resurrection and say: This is what you gave us, so we followed what was in it. The correct thing to say about this is that God Almighty meant by His statement:
h
And he who brought the truth and believed in it everyone who called to the oneness of God

, belief in His messengers, and working with what His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent with from among God’s messengers, his followers, and those who believe in him. And it is said that the truth is the Qur’an and the testimony that there is no god but God, and those who believe in it are the believers in the Qur’an from among all of God’s creation, whoever they may be from God’s prophets and his followers. Rather, we said that this is more correct, because the statement of God Almighty:
h
And he who brought the truth and believed in it
follows His statement:
h
Then who is more unjust than he who lies about God and denies the truth when it has come to him

? This is a censure from God of those who slander Him, who deny His revelation and His revelation, and who deny His Oneness. So, what is required after that is to praise those who are different from those who are censured, and they are the ones who called them to the Oneness of God, and described Him with the description that He has, and believed in the revelation and His revelation, and those who were like that on the day this verse was revealed: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions and those who came after them, who in every age and time called to the Oneness of God and the rule of His Book. This is because God Almighty did not specify this description of Himself in this verse to specific individuals, nor to the people of a time and not others. Rather, He described them with a description, then praised them for it, which is bringing the truth and believing in it. So everyone who is like that is included in the whole of this verse if he is from the children of Adam. And the evidence for the correctness of what we have said is that it is also the case in the reading of Ibn Masʿud:
h
And those who brought the truth
h
and believed in it
. This is evident from his reading that the one in his statement,
h
And those who brought the truth
, did not mean a specific one, but rather that what was meant by it was the whole of that description, but it was produced in the singular form, since it was not specified.

x: Some of the Basran linguists have claimed that who in this instance was made to mean a group, like who. What also supports what we have said is his statement,
h
Those are the righteous
. So he made the predicate of who a group, because it is in the meaning of a group. As for those who said about me in his statement,
h
And believed in it

, that it is other than the one who brought the truth, then this statement is far from the intended meaning, because if that were as they said, then the revelation would be and the one who brought the truth, and the one who believed in it are the righteous, so who would be repeated with belief, so that the one who believes would be other than the one who believes. But since it was not repeated, then what is understood from the statement is that belief is an attribute of the one who brought the truth, and there is no basis for the statement other than that. If that is the case, and it is in the meaning of sexual intercourse as we have explained, then the correct interpretation of it is what we have explained.
And His statement:
h
Those are the righteous

, God Almighty says: Those who have this description are those who feared God by believing in His Oneness, disavowing idols and rivals, performing His obligations, and avoiding His sins, so they feared His punishment.

c: As Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
Those are the righteous
, meaning: Beware of polytheism.

evidence.text: And the evidence for the correctness of what we have said is that it is also the case in the reading of Ibn Masʿud: And those who brought the truth and believed in it.

This is evident from his reading that the one in his statement, And those who brought the truth, did not mean a specific one, but rather that what was meant by it was the whole of that description, but it was produced in the singular form, since it was not specified.

x: And His statement:
h
They will have whatever they wish with their Lord

, God Almighty says: They will have with their Lord on the Day of Resurrection whatever their souls desire and their eyes delight in. That is the reward of the doers of good, God Almighty says: This that they will have with their Lord is the reward of those who did good in this world, obeyed God therein, followed His command, and refrained from what He forbade them therein.

God Almighty says: And their Lord will reward these good-doers for their good deeds, so that He may forgive them the worst of what they did in this world, between them and their Lord, because of what they did therein of repentance and turning back from the evil deeds they committed therein.

i: And He will reward them for their reward He says:
x: And He will give them their reward for the best of what they did in this world of what pleases God with them without the worst of it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: And he who brought the truth and believed in it - those are the righteous.

That is, do they have sins? That is, my Lord, yes. For them in it “They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good, that God may remove from them the worst of what they did and reward them according to the best of what they used to do.”

The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful (al-Anfal 8:2)... until he reached and forgiveness (al-Anfal 8:4) so that those who have sins do not despair of not being among them.
And a noble provision (al-Anfal 8:4). And His statement: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women (al-Ahzab 33:35)... until the end of the verse.
The reciters differed in reading
h
Is not God sufficient for His servant
Some of the reciters of Medina and the majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as
h
Is not God sufficient for His servant

in the plural, meaning: Is not God sufficient for Muhammad and the prophets before him, so that their nations would not fear that their gods would harm them? The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa read it as Bikaf Abdu in the singular, meaning:
h
Is not God sufficient for His servant

Muhammad? The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings in the reading of the regions. Whichever one the reader recites, he is correct, because their meanings are correct and they are widely used in the reading of the regions. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad told me, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
Is not God sufficient for His servant
? He said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
Is not God sufficient for His servant
? He said: Yes, by God, God will suffice him, honor him, and grant him victory as He promised him. And His statement:
h
And they frighten you with those besides Him

, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And these polytheists, O Muhammad, frighten you with those besides God, of idols and deities, lest they harm you, because of your disavowal of them and your criticism of them, and God will suffice you in that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And they threaten you with those besides Him, meaning the gods. He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to Sha’b Basqam to break al-Uzza. Its custodian, who was in charge of them, said: O Khalid, I warn you both, for it is so severe that nothing can withstand it. So Khalid walked towards it with an axe and smashed its nose.”

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: And they threaten you with those besides Him, meaning with their gods that they used to worship.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And they frighten you with those besides Him
, he said: They frighten you with their gods besides Him. And His statement:
h
And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no guide

. God Almighty says: And he whom God lets down and leads astray from the path of truth and the path of right guidance - for him there is no guide or directer to the path of truth other than Him, or one who will grant him success in believing in God, believing in His Messenger, and working in obedience to Him.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in reading Is not God sufficient for His servant?

Some of the reciters of Medina and the majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as Is not God sufficient for His servant in the plural, meaning: Is not God sufficient for Muhammad and the prophets before him, so that their nations would not fear that their gods would harm them?
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa read it as Bikaf Abdu in the singular, meaning: Is not God sufficient for His servant Muhammad?
The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings in the reading of the regions.
Whichever one the reader recites, he is correct, because their meanings are correct and they are widely used in the reading of the regions.

x: And whomsoever God guides, there is none to mislead him. He says: And whomsoever God guides to believe in Him and to act according to His Book, there is none to mislead him. He says: There is none to lead him astray from the truth which he is upon to revert to disbelief. Is not God Exalted in Might and Possessor of Retribution? He, the Most High, says: Is not God, O Muhammad, Exalted in Might and Possessor of Retribution from His enemies who deny His Oneness?

God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And if you, O Muhammad, ask these polytheists who equate idols with God, who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, ‘The one who created them is God.’ So when they say that, then say, ‘Have you considered, O people, these idols and deities that you worship besides God? If God intends me harm,’ meaning, severe hardship in my livelihood, can they prevent from me whatever my Lord afflicts me with harm? Or if God intends me mercy,’ meaning, if my Lord intends me to have ease in my livelihood, abundant wealth, and ease and well-being in my body, can they withhold from me whatever He intends to afflict me with that mercy?” He left the answer out because the listener is satisfied with knowing that, and the evidence of what appears in the speech is clear on it. Meaning: They will say, No. So say, “God is sufficient for me against all things other than Him.

Him I worship, and to Him I turn in my affairs, not to anything else. He is sufficient, and in His hand is harm and benefit. Not to idols and statues that can neither harm nor benefit. “In Him do those who trust.” He says: Whoever trusts puts his trust in God, and let him trust in Him, not in anyone else. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth

, they will surely say, ‘God.’ Until he reached removers of His distress, meaning: the idols. Or did He intend mercy for me? Are they withholding His mercy? There was a difference in the reading of Kashifaat Darah and Muskaat Rahmatu.

x: Some of them read it with the addition and lowering of Darah and Rahmah, while some of the readers of Medina and the majority of the readers of Basra read it with the tanween and lowering Darah and Rahmah. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings with similar meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. It is similar to his saying, The plot of the disbelievers in the case of addition and tanween.

evidence.text: There was a difference in the reading of Kashifaat Darah and Muskaat Rahmatu.

Some of them read it with the addition and lowering of Darah and Rahmah, while some of the readers of Medina and the majority of the readers of Basra read it with the tanween and lowering Darah and Rahmah.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people, who have taken idols and statues as gods to worship besides God: Work, O people, to enable you to do the work that you do and your homes.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: in your place he said: on your side. I am working like that slowly, according to the work of those who came before me from the prophets of God. Then you will know when God’s punishment comes to you, who among us is right and who is wrong, and who is right and who is astray.

x: And His statement:
h
Whoever is afflicted with a punishment God Almighty says

: Whoever is afflicted with a punishment that humiliates him, whatever comes to him of that punishment, meaning that it humiliates and degrades him, and a lasting punishment descends upon him meaning: and a lasting punishment descends upon him that does not leave him.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: “Indeed, We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, the Book as clarification for the people of the truth. “And whoever is guided, it is for [the benefit of] himself.” He says: Whoever acts according to what is in the Book that We sent down to you and follows it, it is for himself. He says: He only acts in that for himself, and seeks good for himself and nothing else, because it brings him the pleasure of God and the attainment of Paradise and salvation from the Fire. And whoever goes astray He says: Whoever deviates from the Book that We sent down to you and the clarification that We made clear to you, strays from the straight path and strays from the right way, then he is only being unjust to himself, and to him is brought ruin and destruction, because he brings him the wrath of God and to them is His punishment and eternal disgrace.
h
And you are not a guardian over them

. God Almighty says: And you, O Muhammad, are not a watcher over those to whom We sent you, watching their deeds and recording their actions. You are only a messenger, and your duty is only to convey, and it is up to Us to hold them to account.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you are not a guardian over them
meaning a guardian.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you are not a guardian over them
, he said: A guardian.

x: God Almighty says: And among the proofs that divinity belongs to the One, the Compeller, and is exclusive to all others, is that He causes death and brings to life, and does what He wills, and nothing else has the power to do that. So He made that a piece of report by which He alerted them to the greatness of His power, saying:
h
God takes the souls at the time of their death

, so He takes them when their appointed time comes and their life span ends. He also takes those that did not die in their sleep, just as He takes those that died at their death. He keeps those for whom He has decreed death, He mentioned that the souls of the living and the dead meet in dreams, and as many of them as God wills get to know each other, and when He wants them all to return to their bodies, God keeps the souls of the dead with Him and imprisons them, and sends the souls of the living back to their bodies for a specified term, that is, until their life span ends.
The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding His statement,
h
God takes the souls at the time of their death

... the verse. He said: He brings together the souls of the living and the souls of the dead, and as many of them as God wills to know each other, He keeps those for whom He has decreed death and sends the others back to their bodies.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement:
h
God takes the souls at the time of their death

, he said: The souls are taken when the sleeper is asleep, so his soul is taken during his sleep, and the souls meet each other, the souls of the dead and the souls of the sleeping, and they meet and ask each other questions. He said: The souls of the living are released so that they return to their bodies, and the others want to return, so He detains the ones for whom death has been decreed and sends the others back until a specified term. He said: Until the remainder of their terms.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
God takes the souls at the time of their death

, and those that do not die during their sleep, he said: So sleep is death. He keeps those for whom He has decreed death and sends the others that He has not taken for a specified term. And His statement:
h
Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought

. God Almighty says: Indeed in God’s taking of the soul of the sleeping or the dead and sending it back after this soul returns to its body, and His withholding of another from its body, there is a lesson and admonition for whoever thinks and reflects, and a clarification for him that God gives life to whomever He wills of His creation when He wills, and causes death to whomever He wills when He wills.

x: God Almighty says: Or have these polytheists taken as intercessors for God besides Him their gods whom they worship, who intercede for them with God in their needs? And His statement: Say, ‘Even if they did not possess anything and did not understand?’ God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say, O Muhammad, to them: Do you take these gods as intercessors as you claim, even if they do not possess for you any benefit or harm, and do not understand anything? Say to them: If you worship them for that reason, and they intercede for you with God, then sincerely worship God and single Him out as divinity, for all intercession belongs to Him. No one intercedes with Him except he whom He permits and whose word He is pleased with. And whenever you sincerely worship Him and call upon Him, He will intercede for you. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth.

He says: He has the authority over the heavens and the earth and their dominion, and whatever you worship, O polytheists, besides Him belongs to Him. He says: So worship the king, not the slave who does not possess anything. Then to Him you will be returned. He says: Then to God is your destination, and He will punish you for associating partners with Him if you die in your polytheism. The meaning of the words: To God belongs all intercession. To Him belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. So worship the Owner who owns the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, who has the power to benefit you in this world and to harm you in it, and when you return to Him after your death, for to Him you will return. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Or have they taken intercessors besides God? “The gods.” “Say: Even if they did not possess anything?” The intercession.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: “Say: To God belongs all intercession,” he said: No one intercedes with Him except with His permission.

x: "Say: To God belongs all intercession. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned."

God the Most High says: And when God, the Most High, is singled out for mention, and He is called upon alone, and it is said, There is no god but God, the hearts of those who do not believe in the afterlife and resurrection after death are filled with disgust. And by His statement, be filled with disgust, He means they are repelled by the Oneness of God. And when those besides Him are mentioned, He says: And when the deities that they call upon besides God are mentioned along with God, it is said, Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for, since those who do not believe in the afterlife are pleased and happy with that.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when God alone is mentioned

, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter are filled with aversion: meaning their hearts are repelled and they become arrogant. And when those other than Him are mentioned “the gods” at once they rejoice.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: It was disgusted, he said: It shrank. He said: That was on the day that Al-Najm was recited to them at the door of the Kaaba.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: I felt disgusted, he said: I felt aversion, and when those other than Him are mentioned, their idols.

evidence.text: He said: That was on the day that Al-Najm was recited to them at the door of the Kaaba.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, God is the
h
Creator of the heavens and the earth
h
Knower of the unseen

and the witnessed, which the sight does not see nor the eyes sense, and the witnessed, which the sight of His creation witnesses and their eyes see. You will judge between Your servants, so you will decide between them with truth on the Day when You will gather them to separate the judgment between them, regarding what they used to differ about in this world, in saying about You, and about Your greatness and Your power and other differences among themselves. So on that Day You will judge between us and these polytheists whose hearts are disgusted when You alone are mentioned, but when those other than You are mentioned, they rejoice in the truth. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Creator of the heavens and the earth
, “Creator” means Creator. And regarding His statement,
h
Knower of the unseen
, he said: Whatever is hidden from His servants, He knows it, and what is witnessed means whatever the servants know and witness, and He knows it.

x: God Almighty says: And if these polytheists who wronged themselves had on the Day of Resurrection, all that is on the earth in this world of its wealth and adornment and the like thereof doubled, and He accepted that from them in exchange for themselves, they would have redeemed themselves with all of that in exchange for it, in order to be saved from the evil punishment of God, with which He will punish them on that Day. And it will appear to them from God He says: And it will appear to them on that Day of God’s command and punishment, which He had prepared for them, that which they had not previously thought He had prepared for them.

God Almighty says: And on the Day of Resurrection, the evils of what they had earned in this world will be made clear to these polytheists, when they were given their books in their left hands, and what they used to ridicule will encompass them. It will then become obligatory upon them, and the punishment of God, which the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had promised them in this world for their disbelief in their Lord, will befall them, as they used to ridicule it, denying that it would befall them or touch them, out of their denial of it, and it will encompass them.

God Almighty says: So when a person is afflicted with hardship and distress, he calls upon Us, seeking aid from Us regarding the harm that has befallen him, Then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, meaning: Then when We give him relief from the harm he was in, by replacing the harm with ease and plenty, and the sickness with health and well-being, then he says: I was only given what I was given of ease and plenty in life, and health in the body and well-being, based on knowledge I have, meaning on knowledge from God that I am worthy of it due to my honor and His pleasure with my work with Me, meaning in what I have, just as one says: You are doing well in this matter with Me, meaning in what I think and reckon. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: Then when We bestowed upon him a favor from Us until he reached with knowledge with Me: meaning with goodness with Me.
