c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: If We bestowed upon him a favor from Us, he said: We gave it to him. His saying: I was given it with knowledge means with an honor that he gave me. And His statement: Rather, it is a trial, meaning that God Almighty says: Rather, We gave them that blessing after the hardship they were in as a trial for them: meaning, a calamity with which We tested them, and a test with which We tested them. But most of them, due to their ignorance and bad opinion, do not know, for what reason they were given that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Rather, it is a trial: meaning a calamity.

x: God the Most High says: He said this statement, meaning their statement about the blessing of God which He bestowed upon them while they were polytheists: We gave it to them based on knowledge we have. And those before them meaning: those before the polytheists of Quraysh from the past nations to their messengers, as a denial and mockery of them. And His statement: But what they used to earn did not avail them means: When God’s punishment came to them because of their denial of God’s messengers and their mockery of them, what they used to earn of deeds did not avail them, and that was their worship of idols. He says: Their service to them did not benefit them, and their gods did not intercede for them with God at that time, but they surrendered to them and disowned them.
And His statement:
h
And the evil of what they earned befell them

. He says: So those who said this statement from the past nations were afflicted with the consequences of the evil of what they earned of deeds, so they were hastened to be disgraced in this world, like Qarun who said when he was sent: I have only been given it because of knowledge I have. So God caused the earth to swallow him and his home. And he had no company to help him other than God, nor was he among those who defend themselves. (al-Qasas 28:81) God, the Most High, says: And those who do wrong among these, He says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Those who disbelieved in God, O Muhammad, from your people, and wronged themselves and said this statement, the consequences of the evil of what they earned will also befall them, just as those before them were afflicted by their saying it. And they will not escape.

He says: And they will not escape their Lord, nor will they outrun Him, fleeing on earth from His punishment when it descends upon them, but it will befall them. This is the way of God with those who passed on before, and you will not find any change in the way of God. (al-Ahzab 33:62) So He did that to them. So he brought them shame in this world and killed them with the sword on the day of Badr. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Those before them said it the past nations and those who did wrong from these, he said: from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: God Almighty says: Didn't these people, O Muhammad, know that We removed their hardship and they said: We were only given it because of knowledge from Us that hardship and ease, spaciousness and distress and affliction are in the hand of God, not anyone else? He expands provision for whomever He wills, and restricts it for whomever He wills of His servants, and restricts it, and that this is from God's proofs to His servants, so that they may consider it and remember, and know that the desire for Him and the fear are not in the hands of gods and rivals. Indeed in that are signs He says: Indeed in God's expansion of provision for whomever He wills, and His restriction of it for whomever He wills, there are signs: meaning indications and signs for a people who believe meaning: they believe in the truth, and they acknowledge it when they understand it and know its reality, that the One who does that is God, not anyone else.
The people of interpretation differed as to who was meant by this verse.

Some of them said: It refers to a group of polytheists who, when they were called to believe in God, said: How can we believe when we have committed polytheism, committed adultery, and killed the soul which God has forbidden, and God promises the one who does that the Fire? What good will faith do us when we have already believed? Then this verse was revealed.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me:
m: On the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas: Say, ‘
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves
h
do not despair of the mercy of God

.’ That is because the people of Mecca said: Muhammad claims that he is an idol worshipper, and he called upon another god along with God, and killed the soul that God has forbidden, and he will not be forgiven. So how can we emigrate and become Muslim, when we have worshipped idols, and killed the soul that God has forbidden, and we are people of polytheism? So God revealed:
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves
h
do not despair of the mercy of God

. He says: Do not despair of My mercy, for God forgives all sins. He said: And turn to your Lord in repentance and submit to Him. (al-Zumar 39:54) God only rebukes those with understanding, and what is lawful and unlawful is only for the people of faith. He rebukes them, and He commands them that if one of them transgresses against himself, he should not despair of the mercy of God, and that he should turn back and not delay in repenting from that transgression and sin that he committed. God mentioned in Surah Al Imran the believers when they asked God for forgiveness, and they said: Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our transgression in our conduct and plant firmly our feet. (al-Zumar 39:147) So it should be known that they had been committing transgressions, so He commanded them to repent from their transgressions.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Those who have transgressed against themselves, he said: killing a soul in the pre-Islamic era.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, he said:
m: These three verses were revealed in Medina about Wahshi and his companions:
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves
until His saying: before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abu Sakhr told me, he said:
m: Zaid bin Aslam said, regarding His statement:
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves
h
do not despair of the mercy of God
, he said: It is only for the polytheists.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves until he reached all sins
. He said: It was mentioned to us that people committed great sins in the pre-Islamic era, and when Islam came, they feared that they would not be forgiven, so God called them with this verse:
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves

c: Muhammad told us: Ahmad told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves

, he said: These were the polytheists from Mecca. They said: How can we answer you when you claim that whoever commits adultery, or murders, or associates others with the Most Merciful is doomed and among the people of Hellfire? So we have done all of these deeds. So this verse was revealed about them:
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves
h
do not despair of the mercy of God

… the verse, he said: There were a people among the people of ignorance who were displeased, and when God sent His Prophet, they said: If only we could go to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believe in him and follow him.

x: Some of them said to one another: How will God and His Messenger accept you in His religion? And they said: Shall we not send a man to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? So when they were sent, the Qur’an was revealed: Say, ‘
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves
h
do not despair of the mercy of God
.’ He recited until he reached: so I will be among the doers of good.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: Shatir ibn Shakl and Masruq were sitting together. Shatir said: Either you narrate what you heard from Ibn Mas’ud and I will believe you, or I will narrate it and you will believe me. Masruq said: No, narrate it and I will believe you. He said: I heard Ibn Mas’ud say: The greatest verse of relief in the Qur’an is:
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves
h
do not despair of the mercy of God
. Masruq said: You have spoken the truth.

x: Others said: Rather, what he meant by that was the people of Islam. He said: The interpretation of the statement is: God forgives all sins for whomever He wills. They said: And it is like that in the copy of Abdullah. They said: This verse was revealed about a people whom the polytheists prevented from emigrating and tempted them, so they feared that there would be no repentance for them.
Who said that?

c: Ibrahim bin Saeed Al-Jawhari narrated to us, he said: Yahya bin Saeed Al-Umawi narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: He - meaning Umar - said:
m: We used to say: There is no repentance for one who is tested. They used to say: God will not accept anything from us. We abandoned Islam because of a calamity that befell us after knowing it. Then when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, God revealed about them:
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves
h
do not despair of the mercy of God

... the verse. Umar said: So I wrote it with my own hand, then sent it to Hisham bin Al-As. Hisham said: When it came to me, I began to recite it but did not understand it. Then it occurred to me that it was revealed about us for what we used to say. So I sat on my camel, then I went to Medina.

c: Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, who said:
m: These verses were revealed about ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, and a group of Muslims who had embraced Islam and then been persecuted and tortured, and so they were persecuted. We used to say that God would never accept any ransom or justice from these people. They were people who embraced Islam and then abandoned their religion because of the torture they inflicted upon them. So these verses were revealed, and ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab was a scribe. He said: So he wrote them with his own hand and sent them to ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, al-Walid ibn al-Walid, to those people, and they embraced Islam and emigrated.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Yunus told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said:
m: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: Which verse in the Quran is the most comprehensive? So they began to mention verses from the Quran: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful
r
(An-Nisa’: 110)
and similar verses. Ali said: There is no verse in the Quran that is more comprehensive than
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves
… to the end of the verse.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Azdi, on the authority of Abu Al-Kanud, who said:
m: Abdullah entered the mosque and suddenly he mentioned the Fire and the chains. He said: So he came and stood over his head and said: What is he mentioning? Have you made people despair?
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves
... the verse.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Al-Qurazi, that he said
m: about this verse:
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves
h
do not despair of the mercy of God
, he said: It is for all people.

c: Zakariya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Zaida narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahi’ah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Qanbal,
m: saying: I heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muzani say: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Jala’i narrated to me that he heard Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘I would not like to have the world and everything in it in exchange for this verse: “
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves
h
do not despair of the mercy of God

...’… the verse. A man said: ‘O Messenger of God, who has associated partners with God?’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent, then he said: ‘Beware of those who have associated partners with God, beware of those who have associated partners with Surat al-Zumar 39:53 Say, "
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves
h
do not despair of the mercy of God
. Indeed, God forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful." God,’ three times.”

x: Others said: This was revealed about a people who saw the people of major sins as people of Hell, so God informed them that He forgives all sins to whomever He wills.
He who mentioned that said:

c: Ibn al-Barqi told me: Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us: Abu Muadh al-Khurasani told us, on the authority of Muqatil ibn Hayyan, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said:
m: We, the companions of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), used to see or say that none of our good deeds were acceptable, until this verse was revealed: Obey God and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds
r
(Muhammad 74:33)

. When this verse was revealed, we said: What is it that invalidates our deeds? We said: Major sins and immoralities. He said: Whenever we saw someone committing any of these, we would say: He is doomed, until this verse was revealed: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills
r
(An-Nisa’ 4:48)

. When this verse was revealed, we refrained from speaking about that, and whenever we saw someone commit any of these, we would fear for him, but if he did not commit any of them, we would hope for him. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: God Almighty meant by that all those who transgress against themselves from among the people of faith and polytheism, because God included in His saying:
h
O My servants who have transgressed against themselves all transgressors
, and He did not specify one transgressor over another.

x: Does God forgive polytheism?
Yes, if the polytheist repents from it.

What is meant by His statement, Indeed, God forgives all sins, is for whomever He wills, as we mentioned before that Ibn Mas’ud used to recite it, and that God excepted from it polytheism if its perpetrator did not repent from it, so He said:
Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills.

So He informed that polytheism is not forgiven except after repentance, as He said: Except for he who repents, believes, and does righteousness. As for what is other than that, its perpetrator is subject to the will of his Lord. If He wills, He will bestow His favor upon him and forgive him, and if He wills, He will be just toward him and reward him for it. As for his saying:
h
Do not despair of the mercy of God
, he means: Do not lose hope in the mercy of God.
Likewise, Muhammad bin Saad told me:

c: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas.
m: We have mentioned the narrations on this matter before and explained its meaning. His statement: Indeed, God forgives all sins means that God covers up all sins by forgiving their people and leaving them unpunished for them if they repent from them. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful towards them, if He punishes them for them after they repent from them.

evidence.text: Hisham said: When it came to me, I began to recite it but did not understand it.

What is meant by His statement, Indeed, God forgives all sins, is for whomever He wills, as we mentioned before that Ibn Mas’ud used to recite it, and that God excepted from it polytheism if its perpetrator did not repent from it, so He said:

x: God Almighty says: And come, O people, to your Lord with repentance, and return to Him with obedience to Him, and respond to what He has called you to of His Oneness, the singling out of divinity, and the devotion of worship to Him alone.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And turn to your Lord means turn to your Lord

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And repent. He said: Answer.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And turn to your Lord in repentance
, he said: Turning means returning to obedience and abandoning what they were doing. Do you not see that He says: Turning to Him and fearing Him (al-Rum 30:31). And His statement:
h
And submit to Him
means:
h
And submit to Him

in obedience and acknowledgment of the true religion before the punishment comes to you from Him for your disbelief in Him and then you will not be helped means: Then no helper will help you, and save you from His punishment that has descended upon you.

x: And His statement:
h
And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord

. God Almighty says: And follow, O people, what your Lord has commanded you to do in His revelation, and avoid what He has forbidden you in it, and that is the best of what was revealed to us from our Lord. If someone were to say: Is there something in the Qur’an that is better than something else? He would be told: “The entire Qur’an is good, and its meaning is not what you imagined. Rather, its meaning is: ‘And follow what your Lord has revealed to you of commands and prohibitions, information, examples, stories, arguments, promises, and threats. The best of it is that you obey His command and refrain from what He has forbidden, because the prohibition is among what was revealed in the Book. If they acted upon what they were forbidden, they would be acting upon the worst of it.’ So that is its meaning.” And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord
meaning: what you were commanded to do in the Book before the punishment comes to you. His statement:
h
Before the punishment comes upon you suddenly
means: Before the punishment of God comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive means: And you do not know about it until it suddenly overtakes you.

x: God Almighty says: And turn to your Lord and submit to Him. “Lest a soul should say” means: Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God. This is similar to His statement: And He has cast into the earth firm mountains, lest it should shake with you (al-Nahl 16:15), meaning: so that it should not shake with you, for if that is the meaning, it is in the accusative case. His saying: Oh, my regret means to say: Oh, my remorse.

c: Muhammad bin al-Husayn told me, he said: Ahmad bin al-Mufaddal told me, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O my regret
, it is a pronoun for the speaker, and what is meant is:
h
O my regret

, but the Arabs change the ya’ in the pronoun for the speaker’s name in the cry for help to an alif, so they say: O woe to us, and O remorse, and they make that into the form of a supplication, and it may be said: O regret for the servants, just as it is said: O sorrow, and O sorrow for him, and al-Farra’ mentioned that Abu Tharwan recited to him: You visit her, but I do not visit your women. I yearn for the sons of the slave girls. In lowering, as it is lowered in calling when the speaker adds it to himself, and they may insert the ha’ after this alif, so they lower it sometimes, and raise it sometimes. Al-Farra’ mentioned that some of Banu Asad recited: Oh God, oh God, I ask you, oh God, before the appointed time Lowering, he said: Lowering is more common in their speech, except in their saying: Ya Hanah, and Ya Hantah, because raising in them is more common than lowering, because it is common in speech, until it became as if it were a single letter. His saying: For what I neglected in the side of God means: For what I wasted in doing what God commanded me to do, and what I fell short in obeying God in this world. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Oh, how I regret what I neglected in the matter of God, he said: in the matter of God.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: For what you neglected in the matter of God, he said: in the matter of God.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: For what I neglected in the matter of God, he said: What I left of the command of God. His saying:
h
And if you were among the mockers

, means: And if you were among those who mock the command of God, His Book, His Messenger, and the believers in Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
That a soul should say

, ‘Oh, how I wish I had neglected my duty to God and had been among the mockers.’ He said: It was not enough for him to neglect the obedience to God, so he began to mock the people who obeyed God. He said: This is the statement of a group of them.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And if you were among the mockers
, meaning: among those who mock the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Book, and what it brought.

x: God Almighty says: And turn to your Lord, O people, and submit to Him, so that no soul will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God, in the matter of God, and that no other soul will say: If only God had guided me to the truth and granted me success in the right path, I would have been among those who feared Him by obeying Him and following what pleases Him, or that no other soul will say when it sees God’s punishment and witnesses it, If only I had a chance, saying: If only I had a return to the world, “so I could be among the doers of good,” those who did good in obeying their Lord and doing what the Messengers commanded them to do. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God… the verse. He said: This is what one group of them said: Or you say, ‘If only God had guided me’… the verse. He said: This is what another group said: Or you say, when you see the punishment’… the verse. He meant by his saying: If only I had another chance a return to the world. He said: This is another group.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
That a soul should say

, ‘Oh, how I wish I had been more negligent in my duty to God,’ He said: God informed us of what the servants would say before they said it, and of their deeds before they did them. He said: And none informs you like the All-Knowing
r
(Fatir 35:14)
h
That a soul should say

, ‘Oh, how I wish I had been more negligent in my duty to God,’ “or should say, ‘If only God had guided me,’”… to His statement, then I would have been among the doers of good, meaning: among the guided. So God, the Exalted, informed us that if they were returned, they would not be able to attain guidance. He said: And if they were returned, they would certainly return to that from which they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars. (al-An’am 6:28), and He said: And We will turn away their hearts and their eyes just as they did not believe in it the first time. (al-An’am 6:110), he said: If they were returned to this world, guidance would be prevented between them, just as We prevented them from it the first time while they were in this world. There are two views on the accusative case of his saying: So I will be. The first is that it is accusative as a response to if. The second is as a response to the position of the ball, and directing the ball in meaning to: If I could repeat, as the poet said: You have nothing of it but memory and regret, and you ask about its riders, where they headed. So he put the word tas’al in the accusative case, in apposition to the place of the mention, because the meaning of the statement is: So why is he sending in the place of the revelation in his statement: except a revelation.

x: Or you will say when you see the punishment, If only I had another chance so I could be among the doers of good.

God Almighty says, refuting the one who says: If God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous, and the one who says: If only I had another chance so I could be among the righteous, the statement is not like what you say: Yes, My signs have come to you, O you who wish to be returned to the world so that you would be among the righteous, “He says: My proofs have come to you from among a Messenger whom I sent to you, and a Book which I revealed in which is recited to you what is in it of promise, threat, and reminder. “But you denied” My signs and were arrogant about accepting and following them, “and you were among the disbelievers,” He says: You were among those who do the work of the disbelievers, follow their example, and adhere to their way. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: God says in response to their statement and as a refutation of them, meaning the statement of those who say, If God had guided me, and the other group: Yes, indeed My signs have come to you... the verse. And with the fatha on the kaf and the ta’ in His statement,
h
My signs came to you

, but you denied, as if addressing males, the reciters in all parts of Islam read it. It has been narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he read it with the kasra of the entire letter, as if he said: That a soul should say, Oh, how I regret what I neglected in the service of God! Yes, indeed My signs have come to you, O soul, but you denied them. He directed the entire statement to the soul, since the statement began with it. The reading that I do not permit a contradiction to it is what the reciters of all parts have agreed upon, transmitted on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is the fatha in all of that.

evidence.text: God Almighty says, refuting the one who says: If God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous, and the one who says: If only I had another chance so I could be among the righteous, the statement is not like what you say: Yes, My signs have come to you, O you who wish to be returned to the world so that you would be among the righteous, “He says: My proofs have come to you from among a Messenger whom I sent to you, and a Book which I revealed in which is recited to you what is in it of promise, threat, and reminder.
And with the fatha on the kaf and the ta’ in His statement, My signs came to you, but you denied, as if addressing males, the reciters in all parts of Islam read it.

It has been narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he read it with the kasra of the entire letter, as if he said: That a soul should say, Oh, how I regret what I neglected in the service of God!

The reading that I do not permit a contradiction to it is what the reciters of all parts have agreed upon, transmitted on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is the fatha in all of that.

x: God Almighty says: “And on the Day of Resurrection you will see, O Muhammad, those who lied about God from among your people, claiming that He had a son and that He had a partner, and worshipped gods other than Him, their faces will be blackened.” Even though the faces are raised by blackened, they have an accusative meaning because they are with their predicate, the completion of you will see. If His saying blackened had come before the faces, it would have been accusative.

i: If the accusative of the blackened faces was an accusative in speech, not in the Qur’an, if the blackened was after, it would have been permissible, as the poet said:
x: Leave me alone, for your command will not be obeyed, and you will not find my patience doubled.

The dream and the doubled letters are accusatives of al-fa-ta’ib I found you, and the Arabs do the same in everything that needs a subject and a predicate, such as dhan and its sisters. In masawdah the Arabs have two dialects: masawdah and maswadah, and it is used by the people of Hijaz, as it is mentioned about them, they say qad aswad wajh his face turned black, ahmar red, and ashhab brown.

Some of the grammarians of Basra mentioned that one of them said: Afa’al only applies to things of one color, such as ashhab. He said: It is not used in things like “ahmar red, because ashhab is a newly occurring color, while ahmar does not. His statement,
h
Is there not in Hell a place of refuge for the arrogant
? means: Is there not in Hell a shelter and a dwelling place for those who are arrogant towards God, and refuse to believe in His Oneness and to obey Him in what He has commanded and forbidden.

God Almighty says: And God will save from Hell and its torment those who fear Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins in this world, by their success: meaning by their victory, and it is an active participle from Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that, even though the words of some of them differed from the wording we said in that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad told me, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God will save those who fear Him by their attainment
, he said: by their virtues.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And God will save those who feared Him with their attainment

, he said: with their deeds. He said: And the others will bear their burdens on the Day of Resurrection, “and from the burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.” (al-Nahl 16:25) The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina, and some of the reciters of Mecca and Basra, read it as bi-mafazatihum in the singular. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as bi-mafazatihum in the plural. What is correct in my opinion regarding this matter is that they are two widely-used readings, and each of them has been recited by scholars among the reciters, so whichever of them the reciter recites is correct, because their meanings are the same. The Arabs sometimes make such a thing singular and plural with one meaning, so one of them says: I heard the voice of the people, and I heard their voices, as God Almighty said: Indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the braying of donkeys
r
(Luqman 31:19)
. He did not say: the voices of donkeys. If it had come like that, it would have been correct. And His statement:
h
No harm will touch them

, nor will they grieve. God Almighty says: The righteous will not be touched by any harm from Hell, which is the harm that God Almighty has informed us will not touch them, nor will they grieve. He says: Nor will they grieve over what they have missed of the pleasures of this world, as they have attained God’s honor and the blessings of Paradise.

evidence.text: (al-Nahl 16:25) The reciters differed in their reading of this.
The majority of the reciters of Medina, and some of the reciters of Mecca and Basra, read it as bi-mafazatihum in the singular.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as bi-mafazatihum in the plural.

What is correct in my opinion regarding this matter is that they are two widely-used readings, and each of them has been recited by scholars among the reciters, so whichever of them the reciter recites is correct, because their meanings are the same.

x: And His statement:
h
God is the Creator of all things and He is Disposer of affairs over all things

. God Almighty says: God, who has divinity over all of His creation and who alone deserves worship, is the Creator of all things, not that which is capable of creating anything, and He is Disposer of affairs over all things. He says: He is the Guardian over all things through preservation and guardianship.

God Almighty says: He has the keys to the treasures of the heavens and the earth. He opens them to whomever He wills and withholds them from whomever He loves among His creation. The singular is: muqalid. As for iqlid, it is the singular of aqalid. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
The keys of the heavens and the earth means their keys

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
He has the keys of the heavens and the earth meaning the keys of the heavens and the earth

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He has the keys of the heavens and the earth
, he said: The treasuries of the heavens and the earth.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth
, he said: The keys are the keys. He said: To Him belong the keys to the treasuries of the heavens and the earth. And His statement:
h
And those who disbelieve in the signs of God - it is they who are the losers

. God Almighty says: And those who disbelieve in the proofs of God, denying them and rejecting them - it is they who are deceived in their share of the best of the heavens, whose keys are in His hand, because they are deprived of all of that in the Hereafter by their eternity in the Fire, and in this world by their failure to believe in God Almighty.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people, who call you to worship idols, Do you command me to worship other than God, O you who are ignorant of God? And worship is not appropriate for anything other than Him. The Arabists differed about the factor in his saying: Afghair the accusative.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: "Say, 'Afghair God ta'amrooni,' meaning: "Afghair God ta'amrooni," as if he wanted to cancel it, and God knows best, just as you say: "He went, so because he knew," making it mean: "So he did not know."

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: "It is not accusative with 'a'bd,' and that it should be deleted and inserted, because it is a proper noun for the future, just as you say: I want to hit, and I want to hit, and Perhaps I hit, and Perhaps I hit, so it was in its request for the future, like you say: Zayd, I will hit, so that is why it was deleted and what came after it worked on what came before it, and we have no need for euphemism.
And His statement:
h
And it has already been revealed to you
, O Muhammad, and to those before you means:
h
And it has already been revealed to you

, O Muhammad, and to those before you of the messengers, If you should associate [anything] with God, your work will surely become worthless meaning: If you, O Muhammad, associate anything with God, your work will surely become worthless, and you will not receive any reward for it, and you will not attain any recompense other than the recompense of those who associate [anything] with God. This is from the deferred meaning of the forward, and the meaning of the statement:
h
And it has already been revealed to you

, If you should associate [anything] with God, your work will surely become worthless, and you will surely be among the losers, and to those before you, meaning: And to those before you of the messengers, of that, like what was revealed to you of it, so beware of associating anything with God and thus you will perish. The meaning of his saying:
h
And you will surely be among the losers is that you will surely be among those who perish by associating partners with God
, if you associate anything with Him.

God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Do not worship what these polytheists of your people have ordered you to worship, O Muhammad. Rather, worship God alone, and not all other gods, idols, and rivals to Him. And be among the grateful to God for His blessings upon you by bestowing guidance to His worship and disavowing the worship of idols and statues. The name of God is in the accusative case by His statement:
h
Worship which comes after it

, because it is a response to a statement. If it had been in the accusative case with an implied noun before it, since the Arabs used to say: Zaid, let him stand, and Zaid, let him stand, in the nominative and accusative cases. The nominative case is based on Let Zaid look, let him stand, and the accusative case is based on Look, Zaid, let him stand, it would have been correct and permissible.

And His statement: And they have not appreciated God as He should be appreciated. God Almighty says: And these polytheists who call you to worship idols have not glorified God as He should be glorified. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And they did not appraise God with His true appraisal. He said: They are the disbelievers who did not believe in God’s power over them. So whoever believes that God is capable of everything, then he has appraised God with His true appraisal, and whoever does not believe in that, then he has not appraised God with His true appraisal.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: And they did not appreciate God with His true appreciation: they did not glorify God with His true greatness. And His statement:
h
And the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection
, God Almighty says:
h
And the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection

, and the heavens, all of them, will be folded in His right hand. So the report about the earth ends with His statement: on the Day of Resurrection, and the earth is raised by His statement: in His grip. Then He resumes the report about the heavens, saying: and the heavens will be folded in His right hand, and they are raised by what is folded.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and a group of others
m: that they used to say: The earth and the heavens will all be in his right hand on the Day of Resurrection.
b.via: Ibn Abbas and a group of others

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the entire earth will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection

, meaning: He has grasped the entire earth and the heavens in His right hand. Have you not heard that He said: Folded in His right hand, meaning: The earth and the heavens in His right hand, all together? Ibn Abbas said: He only seeks help with his left hand, which is occupied by his right hand.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muadh bin Hisham told us: My father told me on the authority of Amr bin Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Juza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The seven heavens and the seven earths in the hand of God are like a mustard seed in the hand of one of you. He said: Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said:

c: My father told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Al-Nadr bin Anas told us, on the authority of Rabia Al-Jarsi, he said:
m: h
And the entire earth will be in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection
, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. He said: And His other hand will be empty, with nothing in it.

c: Ali bin Al-Hassan Al-Azdi told me: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Amara bin Amr, on the authority of Al-Hassan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the entire earth will be in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection
, he said: It will be like a walnut, its parts and its tops.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And the entire earth will be in His grip on the Day of Surat al-Zumar 39
:67 And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand.
h
Glory be to Him

, and He is far above what they associate with Him. Resurrection, that he said: The heavens and the earth will be folded in His right hand, all together. Ibn Abbas used to say: He only seeks help from his left hand, which is occupied by his right hand, and the earth and the heavens are all in his right hand, and there is nothing in his left hand.

c: Al-Rabi’ narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Usamah ibn Zayd informed me, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar,
m: “That he saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the pulpit delivering a sermon to the people, and he passed by this verse: ‘And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He will take the seven heavens and the earths and place them in His hand, then he will say with them as a boy says with a ball: ‘I am God, the One, I am God, the Almighty.’ So we saw the pulpit and he was about to fall down with it.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said: Mansur and Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ubaydah al-Salmani, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: “A Jew came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Muhammad, God holds the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the mountains on one finger, and the creation on one finger, then He says: I am the King.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed until his molars were visible and said: ‘They have not appraised God as He should be appraised.’”

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us: Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed in amazement and belief.” Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated: Asbat narrated from al-Suddi, from Mansur, from Khaithamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Alqamah, from Abdullah ibn Masʿud, who said: “We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when one of the Jewish rabbis came to him and sat next to him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘Tell us.’ He said: ‘When the Day of Resurrection comes, God, the Blessed and Exalted, will place the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the mountains on one finger, the water and the trees on one finger, and all of creation on one finger. Then He will shake them and say: I am the King.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed until his molars could be seen in confirmation of what he had said. Then he recited this verse: ‘And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal…’” Muhammad told us:

c: Ahmad told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: something similar.

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Abbas ibn Abi Talib told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: “A Jew passed by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting, and said: ‘O Jew, tell us.’ He said: ‘How do you say, O Abu al-Qasim, about the Day when God will place the heavens on this side, the earth on this side, the mountains on this side, and the rest of creation on this side?’ Then God revealed: ‘And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal…’ the verse.”

c: Abu al-Sa'ib told me: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: "A man from among the People of the Book came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: 'O Abu al-Qasim, has it reached you that the creation can be carried on one finger, the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the trees on one finger, and the soil on one finger?' The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed until his molars could be seen, and then God revealed: 'But they have not appraised God with true appraisal, while the earth entirely is in His grasp...'...to the end of the verse."

x: Others said: Rather, the heavens are in his right hand, and the earths are in his left.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Dawud told us: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Ibn Abi Hazim told us: Abu Hazim told me on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Muqsim
m: that he heard Abdullah bin Umar say: “I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on the pulpit saying: The Almighty will take hold of His heavens and His earth with His hands - and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, closed his hands and opened them and closed them - then he said: The Most Gracious, I am the King. Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant ones? And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, swayed to his right and to his left, until I saw the pulpit moving from the bottom of a part of it, until I thought: Is it falling with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?”

c: Abu Alqamah Al-Farawi Abdullah bin Muhammad narrated to me, he said: Abdullah bin Nafi’ narrated to me, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, that he said:
m: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘The Compeller will take hold of His heavens and His earth in His hand.’ And he clenched his hand and began to close it and open it, then he said: ‘I am the Compeller, I am the King. Where are the Compellers, where are the arrogant ones?’ He said: ‘The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would lean to his right and to his left, until I saw the lamp moving from under a part of it, until I said: ‘Is it falling with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?’”

c: Al-Hasan bin Ali bin Ayyash Al-Himsi told me, he said: Bishr bin Shuaib told us, he said: My father told us, he said: Muhammad bin Muslim bin Shihab told us, he said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told me, on the authority of Abu Hurairah
m: that he used to say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty will seize the earth on the Day of Resurrection and fold the heavens with His right hand, then He will say: I am the King. Where are the kings of the earth?”

c: It was narrated on the authority of Harmalah bin Yahya,
m: who said: Idris bin Yahya al-Qa’id narrated to us, who said: Haywah informed us, on the authority of Aqil, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: Nafi’, the freed slave of Ibn Umar, informed me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will grasp the earth in His hand on the Day of Resurrection, and fold the heavens and say, ‘I am the King.’”

c: Muhammad ibn Awn told me: Abu al-Mughira told us: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Saeed ibn Thauban al-Kila’i told us on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari:
m: “A Jewish rabbi came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Have you seen when God says in His Book: “
h
And the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection
, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand,” then where will creation be in that case? He said: They will be in it like numbers in a book.”

c: Ibrahim bin Saeed Al-Jawhari told us: Abu Usamah told us: Amr bin Hamza told us: Salim told us, on the authority of his father,
m: “that he told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will fold the heavens and seize them with His right hand, and fold the earth and seize it with His left, then He will say: I am the King. Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?” It was said: This verse was revealed because of a Jew who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the description of God.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Saʿid, who said:
m: “A group of Jews came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Muhammad, God created creation, so who created Him?’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, became so angry that his face turned pale, and then he complained to them in anger for the sake of his Lord. Then Gabriel came to him and calmed him down and said: ‘Lower your wing, O Muhammad, and the answer to what they had asked him came to him from God. He said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, says: “Say: He is God, the One. God, the Self-Sufficient. He neither begets nor is born. And there is none comparable to Him.” (al-Ikhla 112:1-4) When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it to them, they said: ‘Describe to us your Lord! How did He create Him, how did He support Him, and how did He fortify Him?’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, became even more angry than the first time, and then he complained to them, and Gabriel came to him and said the same as he had said, and came to him with the answer to what they had asked him about: ‘And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection. ’” And the heavens are folded in His right hand.
h
Glory be to Him
, and He is far above what they associate with Him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid, who said:
m: The Jews spoke about the description of the Lord, and they said what they did not know and did not see. So God revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal. Then He explained to the people His greatness, saying: “And the earth entirely will be in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand.
h
Glory be to Him
, and He is exalted above what they associate with Him.” So He made the description with which they described God an act of polytheism.

x: Some of the Arab scholars from Basra said: And the earth entirely will be in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. He is talking about His power, similar to His statement:
h
And what your right hands possess (An-Nisa’

: 36), meaning, what you have power over. The right hand does not possess power to the exclusion of the rest of the body. He said: His statement His grasp is similar to your saying to a man, This is in your hand and in your grasp. The reports that we have mentioned from the Messenger of God, his companions, and others, testify to the length of this statement.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Harun ibn al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Umrah, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Aisha, who said:
m: “I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about His statement: ‘
h
And the entire earth will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection
.’ So where will the people be on that Day? He said: ‘On the Bridge.’” And His saying:
h
Glory be to Him

, and He is exalted above what they associate with Him. God Almighty says, sanctifying and exonerating God, and exalting Him and being above what these polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, associate with Him, who say to you: Worship idols instead of God, and prostrate to our gods.

evidence.text: Then he recited this verse: ‘And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal…’” Muhammad told us:
(al-Ikhla 112:1-4) When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it to them, they said: ‘Describe to us your Lord!

x: God Almighty says: And Israfil will blow the trumpet. We have already explained the meaning of the trumpet with supporting evidence, and we have mentioned the differences of opinion among scholars regarding it and the correct opinion regarding it with supporting evidence, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. And His saying,
h
Then everyone in the heavens and on the earth fell unconscious
, means: died, and that was at the first blast.

c: Muhammad told us: Ahmad told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and on the earth will fall unconscious. He said: He died. And His statement:
h
Except whom God wills

x: The people of interpretation differed about who God meant by the exception in this verse.
Some of them said: He meant Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: And the Trumpet will be blown, and everyone in the heavens and on the earth will fall unconscious,
h
except whom God wills
. He said: Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death.

c: Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm told me: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharibi told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us: al-Fadl ibn Isa told us, on the authority of his paternal uncle Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will fall unconscious,
h
except whom God wills

. ’ It was said: ‘Who are these whom God has excepted, O Messenger of God? ’ He said: ‘Gabriel, Michael, and the Angel of Death. ’ When he takes the souls of the creation, he says: ‘O Angel of Death, who remains?’ And He knows best. ’ He said: ‘He says: ‘Glory be to You, blessed are You, my Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor. Gabriel, Michael, and the Angel of Death remain. ’ He said: ‘He says: O Angel of Death, take the soul of Michael. ’ He said: ‘So he falls like a great mountain. ’ He said: ‘Then he says: O Angel of Death, who remains? ’ He says: ‘Glory be to You, my Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honor. Gabriel and the Angel of Death remain. ’ He said: ‘Then he says: O Angel of Death, die. ’ He said: ‘So he dies. ’ He said: ‘Then he says: O Gabriel, who remains? ’ He said: Gabriel will say: Glory be to You, my Lord, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor. Gabriel remains. He is with God in the place where he is. He will say: O Gabriel, he must die. He will fall down in prostration, flapping his wings, saying: Glory be to You, my Lord, blessed and exalted are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor. You are the Everlasting, and Gabriel is the dead, mortal. He will take his soul in the ring from which he was created. He will say: It will come to Michael that the superiority of his creation over the creation of Michael is like the superiority of a great mountain over a small mountain.

x: Others said that he meant the martyrs.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said: Wahb ibn Jarir told me, he said: Shu’bah ibn ‘Amara told us, on the authority of Dhi Hajar al-Yahmadi, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding His statement: “
h
Then everyone in the heavens and the earth will fall unconscious except whom God wills
,” he said: The martyrs are the ones who are around the Throne of God, wearing swords.

x: Others said: The exception in the case of terror is meant to be the martyrs, and in the case of the shock it is meant to be Gabriel, the Angel of Death, and the bearers of the Throne. Mention who said that, and the report that he brought from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Kurayb narrated: Al-Muharibi Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’ al-Madani, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The Trumpet will be blown three times: the first will be the blast of terror, the second will be the blast of the stun, and the third will be the blast of the rising of the Lord of the Worlds, Blessed and Exalted be He.

God will command Israfil with the first blast, and he will say: ‘Blow the blast of terror.’ So the people of the heavens and the earth will be terrified, except for whom God wills.’ Abu Hurayrah said: ‘O Messenger of God, who made an exception when He says: “So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except for whom God wills.”’ He said: ‘Those are the martyrs, and terror will only reach the living. They are alive with their Lord, provided for. God has protected them from the terror of that Day and made them safe. Then God will command Israfil with the blast of the stun, and he will say: ‘Blow the blast of the stun,’ so the people of the heavens will be terrified.’” And the earth except for whom God wills, and behold, they will be extinct. Then the Angel of Death will come to the Almighty, Blessed and Exalted be He, and will say: O Lord, the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth have died except for whom You will.

He will say to him, and He is All-Knowing: Who remains? He will say: You, the Ever-Living Who does not die, remain, and the bearers of Your Throne remain, and Gabriel and Michael remain. God will say to him: Be quiet, for I have decreed death for whoever is beneath My Throne. Then the Angel of Death will come and say: O Lord, Gabriel and Michael have died. God will say, and He is All-Knowing: Who remains? He will say: You, the Ever-Living Who does not die, remain, and the bearers of Your Throne remain, and I remain. God will say: Let the bearers of the Throne die, and they will die. God will command the Throne to seize the Trumpet, and it will say: O Lord, the bearers of Your Throne have died. He will say: Who remains? He is All-Knowing: He will say: You, the Ever-Living Who does not die, remain, and I remain. God will say: You are of My creation; I created you for what You saw, so die and you will not live again, and he will die.

This statement, which was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more likely to be true, because the shock in this case means death. And even though the martyrs are alive with God, as God, the Most High, has stated, they have already tasted death before that. Rather, what He, the Most High, meant by the exception in this place was the exception of those who were struck dead at the blast of the trumpet, not of those who had died before that by a long time and age. This is because if it were possible that what was meant by that was someone who had perished and tasted death before the time of the blast of the trumpet, then what was meant by that would have to be someone who had perished and experienced death before that, because he is one of those who would not be struck dead at that time if the dead person does not experience another death in that situation.
Others said about this:

c: What Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then everyone in the heavens and the earth will fall unconscious except whom God wills

, Al-Hasan said: God makes an exception and does not leave anyone from the people of the heavens or the earth without making him taste death. Qatada said: God has made an exception, and God knows best, to what his front tooth became. He said: “It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God said: An angel came to me and said: O Muhammad, choose a prophet-king, or a prophet-slave. So he gestured to me to be humble. He said: A prophet-slave. So I was given two qualities: that I would be made the first from whom the earth would split open, and the first to intercede. So I would raise my head and find Moses holding the throne. So God knows best whether he fell unconscious after the first shock or not.”

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: “A Jew in the marketplace of Madinah said: ‘By Him Who chose Moses over all mankind,’ then a man from the Ansar raised his hand and struck his face with it, saying: ‘You say this while the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) is among us?’ The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘The Trumpet will be blown and everyone in the heavens and on the earth will fall unconscious
h
except whom God wills

. Then it will be blown again and they will be standing, looking on. Then I will be the first to raise his head, and then Moses will take hold of one of the pillars of the Throne. I do not know whether he will raise his head before me or whether he will be among those whom God has exempted.’”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It is as if I am shaking the dust off my head as I come out. Then I turn around and do not see anyone except Moses clinging to the throne. I do not know whether he is the one whom God has exempted from being blown, or whether he was sent before me.’” And His saying:
h
Then He will blow into it again
, and at once they will be standing, looking on. God Almighty says: Then He will blow into the trumpet another time, and the ha in in it is from the mention of the trumpet.

c: Muhammad told us: Ahmad told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Then he will blow into it again. He said: In the trumpet, and it is the blowing of the resurrection. He mentioned that there will be forty years between the two blasts. It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Between the two blasts there will be forty - they said: O Abu Hurayrah, forty days? He said: I refuse. They said: Forty months? He said: I refuse. They said: Forty years? He said: I refuse. - then God sends down water from the sky and you grow as herbs grow. He said: There is nothing in man that will not decay, except one bone, which is the coccyx, and from it creation will be reconstituted on the Day of Resurrection.”

c: Yahya bin Wadh told us, he said: Al-Balkhi bin Iyas told us, he said:
m: I heard Ikrimah say: Regarding His statement:
h
And everyone in the heavens and the earth fell unconscious
... the verse, he said: The first is from this world, and the last is from the hereafter.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on. “The Prophet of God said: Between the two blasts there will be forty Surat al-Zumar 39:68 And the Trumpet will be blown, and everyone in the heavens and the earth will fall unconscious,
h
except whom God wills

. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on. years.” He said: His companions said: We did not ask him about that, nor did he give us more than that, except that they were of the opinion that it would be forty years. He told us that during those forty days, He sends down rain called the rain of life, until the earth becomes pleasant and quivers, and the bodies of the people grow green plants. Then He blows into it a second time, and behold, they will be standing, looking on. He said: It was told to us that Muadh ibn Jabal asked the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: How will the believers be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection? He said: They will be resurrected hairless, beardless, with kohl-rimmed eyes, thirty years old. And His statement,
h
Then they will be standing

, looking on, means: Then those who were struck dead at the blast before it, and others from all of God’s creation who were dead before that, will rise from their graves and their places on earth, alive as they were before their death, looking on as God’s command concerning them.

c: As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
Then they will be standing
, looking on. He said: When they are resurrected.

x: God Almighty says: Then the earth was illuminated by the light of its Lord. It is said: The sun rose if it became clear and bright, and it rose if it appeared, and that is when the Most Merciful appears to decide the judgment among His creation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord
, he said: So they are not harmed by His light except as they are harmed by the sun on a clear day in which there is no smoke.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord
. He said: It will illuminate. His saying:
h
And the book is placed
means: the book of their deeds for their accountability and punishment.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And the book is placed
, he said: the book of their deeds.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: And the book was placed, he said: the account. And His statement:
h
And the prophets and the martyrs will be brought forth

, meaning: The prophets will be brought forth so that their Lord may ask them about what their nations answered them in this world when the Message of God came to them. And the martyrs, meaning the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will be called by their Lord to witness against the messengers, in what I mentioned about their conveying the Message of God with which their Lord sent them to their nations, if their nations denied that they conveyed the Message of God to them. And martyrs is the plural of martyr, and this is similar to the statement of God: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you.
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:143)

It was said that what is meant by His statement the martyrs are those who were killed in the cause of God. What they said about that in this place does not have much meaning, because after His saying:
h
And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought

, “and it will be judged between them with truth,” and in that is clear evidence of the correctness of what we said, that the prophets and the witnesses were only called to judge between the prophets and their nations, and that the martyrs are all witnesses, who testify for the prophets against their nations as we mentioned. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought
, for they will bear witness for the messengers that they conveyed the message and that the nations denied them.

x: Mention of the one who said what we have mentioned of the other saying:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And the prophets and the martyrs will be brought: those who were martyred in obedience to God. And His statement:
h
And He judged between them with justice

, God Almighty says: And He judged between the prophets and their nations with justice, and His judgment between them with justice is that He does not hold anyone responsible for the sin of another, and He does not punish a soul except for what it has earned.

x: God Almighty says: And at that time God will fully recompense every soul for its deeds of good and evil. He knows best what they do in this world, whether it is obedience or disobedience. Nothing of that is hidden from Him. He will reward them for it on the Day of Resurrection. He will reward the doer of good for his good deeds, and the doer of evil for his evil deeds.
And His statement:
h
And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hellfire
means: And those who disbelieved in God will be gathered to His fire which He has prepared for them on the Day of Resurrection in groups, group by group, and party by party.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: groups, he said: groups. And His statement: Until, when they come to it, its seven gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, “its guardians will say to them: ‘Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord? ’” meaning the Book of God revealed to His Messenger and His proofs with which He sent His messengers to their nations, and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours? He says: And they warn you of what you will encounter on this Day of yours. It may also be possible that its meaning is: And they warn you of your fate until this Day. They said: Yes. He says: Those who disbelieved will say, responding to the keepers of Hell: Yes, messengers from us have come to us, warning us of our meeting on this Day. “But the word of punishment has come to pass upon the disbelievers.” He says: They said: But the word of God has come to pass that His punishment of the people of disbelief in Him is upon us because of our disbelief in Him.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers because of their deeds

x: God Almighty says: Then the keepers of Hell will say to those who disbelieved at that time, ‘Enter the seven gates of Hell,’ according to the number of your stations therein, ‘to abide therein forever.’ That is, remaining there, never moving from it to another place. Then evil is the abode of the arrogant. That is, evil is the abode of those who were arrogant towards God in this world, that they would worship Him alone and single out God for Him alone: Hell on the Day of Resurrection.

God Almighty says: “And those who feared their Lord by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins in this world, and sincerely devoted divinity to Him therein and devoted worship to Him alone, and did not associate anything with Him in their worship, will be gathered to Paradise in groups,” meaning groups. So the driving of these people to their homes in Paradise was a delegation, as we explained before in Surah Maryam, on the best of the best of Paradise, and the driving of the others to Hell was a call and a ritual, as God said.
The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this, and we have mentioned this in its places in this book.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups and regarding His statement: And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, he said: The driving of those was violent, consequential, and pushing. And he recited: The Day they are called to the Fire of Hell, they will be called (al-Tur 52:13), he said: They will be pushed forcefully. And he recited: Then that is he who drives away the orphan (al-Ma’un 107:2), he said: He pushes him. And he recited: And We will drive the criminals to Hell in droves
r
(Maryam 19:86)
- and - We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation
r
(Maryam 19:85)
, then he said: So these are the delegation of God.

c: Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sharik ibn Abdullah informed us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Asim ibn Damrah, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib,
m: may God be pleased with him, regarding His statement:
h
And those who feared their Lord will be led to Paradise in groups

, until, when they reach its door, they see a tree from whose root two springs emerge. They will go to one of them and drink from it as if they were commanded to do so, and whatever was in their bellies of filth, harm, or dirt will come out. Then they will go to the other and perform ablution from it as if they were commanded to do so, and a glimpse of bliss will descend upon them, and their heads will never be disheveled after that, and their clothes will never wear out after that. Then they will enter Paradise, and their parents will meet them as if they were hidden pearls, and they will say: Be of good cheer, God has prepared for you such and such, and has prepared for you such and such. Then they will look at the foundation of its building, and it will be a slew of red, yellow, and green pearls, glittering like lightning. Had God not decreed that their sight would not go, they would have gone. Then some of them will come to their wives, and they will say: Be of good cheer. So-and-so, son of so-and-so, has come. He calls him by his name and his father’s name. She says, Did you see him? Did you see him? Joy overwhelms her until she gets up and sits on the threshold of her door. He enters, reclines on his bed, and recites this verse: “Praise be to God, who has guided us to this. And we would not have been guided had God not guided us.” (al-A’raf 7:43) Muhammad told us:

c: Ahmad told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: Abu Ishaq mentioned on the authority of al-Harith on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: They will be driven to Paradise, and they will reach it and find at its gate a tree at the base of its trunk two springs running. They will go to one of them and wash themselves from it, and the freshness of bliss will flow over them, and their heads will never be disheveled again, and their skins will never be covered with dust, as if they had been anointed with oil. They will go to the other and drink from it, and whatever dirt or harm is in their bellies will go away. Then they will come to the gate of Paradise and ask for admission, and it will be opened for them. The keepers of Paradise will meet them and say: “
h
Peace be upon you

. Enter Paradise for what you used to do.” (al-Nahl 16:32) He said: And the immortal youths will meet them, and they will circle around them as the youths of the people of this world are circled around boiling water when it comes from absence. They will say: Be of good cheer, God has prepared such and such for you, and has prepared such and such for you. Then one of them will go to his wife and give her the good report of him, and he will say: : So-and-so will come forward with the name by which he was called in the world. He said: Joy will overwhelm her until she stands on the threshold of her door and says: Did you see him? Did you see him? He said: He will say: Yes. He said: So he will come until he reaches his home, and when they reach it, they will find it made of pearls of yellow, red and green. He said: So he will enter and there will be cups placed, cushions arranged and carpets spread out. He said: Then he will enter to his wife from among the wide-eyed maidens. Had it not been that God had prepared her for him, his sight would have been dazzled by her light and beauty. He said: So he will recline at that and say, “Praise be to God, Who has guided us to this.
