We would not have been guided had Surat al-Zumar 39:73 And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups until, when they reach it and its gates are opened and its keepers say to them, "
h
Peace be upon you
. You have become good, so enter it to abide eternally." it not been that God guided us.”
r
(Al-A’raf 7:43)
He said: So the angels will call out to them: Indeed, this is Paradise which you have inherited because of what you used to do.
r
(Al-A’raf 7:43)
Muhammad told us, he said:

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, he said:
m: Al-Suddi also mentioned something similar, except that he said: He is more likely to be guided to a position in Paradise than to his position in this world. Then Al-Suddi recited: And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them
r
(Muhammad 47:6)
. The Arab scholars differed about the position of the answer to the verb if in his statement, until they came to it.

x: Some of the Basran grammarians said: It is said that his statement, and its keepers said to them, has the meaning of he said to them, as if he were eliminating the waw.

i: There is something in poetry that seems to suggest that the waw is redundant, as the poet said:
x: So, O Kabisha, this is nothing but a dreamer’s imagination.

It seems that he means: Then that would not have happened. He said: And some of them said: So he omitted the report, and omitting the report is also better in the verse, and omitting the report of speech is common. And another of them said: He is blind to his report, he said: And the Arabs do the same, Abd Manaf bin Rib’ said at the end of the poem: Even if they lead them in a path of sectarian strife, they will be driven away as stray camels are driven away. Al-Akhtal said in the last poem: Except that a tribe of Quraish favored the people or that the noble ones were humiliated.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The waw was inserted into <hatta idha>and <falama>in its response and was removed. As for the one who removed it, there is nothing wrong with it. The one who inserted it likened the first ones to astonishment, so he made the second a sequence to the first, even though the second was a response as if he said: I am astonished by this and this. The first and most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the one that says: The answer is rejected, even though the other saying is not refuted. This is because His statement: “And its keepers will say to them, ‘
h
Peace be upon you
h
you are well

, so enter it to abide therein,’” indicates that there is something omitted in the statement, since it is followed by: And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us.’ If that is the case, then the meaning of the statement is: “Until when they come to it and its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them, ‘
h
Peace be upon you
h
you are well
, so enter it to abide therein,’ they will enter it and say, ‘Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us.’”
What He meant by His statement, “
h
Peace be upon you
,” is security from God for you that you will not be afflicted with any harm or injury after that. His statement,
h
You are well
, means: Your deeds in this world were good, so today your abode is good.
And Mujahid used to say about that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement you were good he said: you were good in obeying God.

evidence.text: He enters, reclines on his bed, and recites this verse: “Praise be to God, who has guided us to this.

x: And His statement: And they said, ‘Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us.’ He says: And those who were led in groups and entered it said: All thanks are due to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us, who had promised them in this world for their obedience to Him, and He fulfilled it by fulfilling it for us today. And He has given us inheritance of the earth. He says: And He made the land of Paradise, which was for the people of Hell, if they had obeyed God in this world and entered it, an inheritance for us from them.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And We caused the earth to be inherited
, he said: the land of Paradise.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And We caused the earth to be inherited
means the land of Paradise.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And We caused the earth to be inherited
, he said: The land of Paradise, and he recited: The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants
r
(Al-Anbiya’: 105)
. His saying:
h
We will settle in Paradise wherever we wish
means: We will take a home in Paradise and live wherever we like and desire.

c: As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
We will settle in Paradise wherever we wish

, we will descend from it whenever we wish. And His saying: The best reward for those who work means: The best reward for those who obey God and work for Him in this world is Paradise for whomever God gives it to in the Hereafter.

x: God Almighty says: And you see, O Muhammad, the angels surrounding the Throne of the Most Merciful. By the Throne, He means the bed.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne
: surrounding it.

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne
. He said: Surrounding the Throne. He said: The Throne is the bed. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the inclusion of <min>in His statement:
h
Hafin min hawal al-‘Arsh
meaning:
h
Hafin min hawal al-‘Arsh
, and in His statement: And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you that if you should associate others with God, your work would surely become worthless (al-Zumar 39:65).

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: “I included <min>in these two places for emphasis, and God knows best, like your saying: No one came to me.”

Another said: Before and around and similar to them are circumstances in which <min>enters and exits, like: I came to you before Zayd, and before Zayd, and We circled around you and around you. This is not of the same type as: No one came to me, because the position of <min>in their statement: No one came to me is nominative, and it is a noun. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that <min>in these places, I mean in His saying: from around the throne and before you, and what is similar to that, and even if it is used with circumstances, then they have the meaning of emphasis. And His saying:
h
They glorify the praises of their Lord

means: They pray around the Throne of God in thanks to Him. The Arabs sometimes insert the letter ba in glorification, and sometimes delete it, so they say: glorify the praise of God, and glorify the praise of God, as God Almighty said: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High (al-A’la 87:1), and He said in another place: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great [al-Waqi’ah 56:74 and 96 - al-Haqqah 69:52].

His statement: And it was judged between them with truth means: And God judged between the prophets who were brought, and the martyrs and their nations with justice. He settled the people of faith in God and in what His messengers brought in Paradise, and the people of disbelief in Him and what His messengers brought in the Fire. And it was said, ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds’ means: And the conclusion of the judgement between them was concluded with thanks to the One who began their creation, to whom belongs divinity and dominion over all that is in the heavens and the earth of creation, from angels, jinn, humans, and other kinds of creation.
Qatada used to say about that:

c: What Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
They glorify the praises of their Lord

... the entire verse. He said: He opened the first creation with praise to God, then said: Praise be to God who created the heavens and the earth, and he concluded with praise and said: “And it was judged between them in truth, and it was said: Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.”
